sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova: A New Generation of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: Dated December 3, 2024; explicitly says Nova Micro, Lite and Pro are generally available today. Identifies Amazon, the Nova family, multimodal Lite, and 300K context.

sources.title: Nova Lite - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: exact model amazon.nova-lite-v1:0; 300K context; text/image/video input, text output and client-side tool calling. No nominal total or active count. Lists launch December 5, 2024, conflicting with the contemporaneous December 3 GA announcement.

sources.title: What is Amazon Nova? - Version 1
sources.evidence: Names Amazon Nova Lite, model ID amazon.nova-lite-v1:0, 300K context, text/image/video input, text output, and PDF document support. Describes fast, low-cost multimodal processing and agentic use cases.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: section 1.1 explicitly identifies Pro, Lite and Micro as Transformer models and describes their pretraining. No numeric total or active count, dense/MoE topology, or named size-disclosed base for Lite is provided. Evaluations do not supply a parameter comparison column.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: service card covers models current April 30, 2025. It identifies Lite modalities and Transformer token inference and describes customized distillation students, but supplies no Lite total/active count or dense/MoE topology. Distillation from Pro/Premier is a customization relationship, not evidence that Lite inherits their size.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: April 30, 2025 addendum describes Premier as a teacher for customized Pro, Lite and Micro. Its capability/runtime comparisons and distillation discussion give no Lite total or active parameter count; teacher/student relationships cannot establish equal nominal size.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: Nova 1 Lite appears in Tables 1-3 and 14. Columns report text, agentic, multimodal and safety benchmark results, with no total/activated parameter column. The report does not disclose Nova 1 Lite total/active parameters or dense/MoE topology.

sources.title: Customize Amazon Nova in Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: July 16, 2025 announcement explicitly classifies the model family as proprietary and names Nova Micro, Nova Lite and Nova Pro in the customization scope.

sources.title: Available foundation models - Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Table dated July 29, 2026 lists Nova Lite, nova-textgeneration-lite, with license AWS Service Terms and inference instances not applicable. The row sits under the broad Open-Weight Models tab, conflicting with AWS explicit proprietary-weight statements; table placement alone is not treated as a weight-release announcement.

sources.title: Iterative Training - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current documentation explicitly states Amazon Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow S3 buckets in AWS-managed accounts instead of being copied to the customer account. Examples use Nova 2, so the exact Nova 1 Lite classification is anchored in the July 2025 announcement.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: exact comparison table lists Nova 1 Lite 300K context and Extended Thinking No versus Nova 2 Lite Yes. Tables cover context, outputs, modalities, thinking, tools and customization, not total or active parameters. Existing reasoning conflict with the v1 schema is preserved.

sources.title: Complete request schema - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current version-1 guide includes reasoningConfig and explicitly labels it Amazon Nova Pro and Amazon Nova Lite only. This conflicts with the model-specific migration table; cannot establish a reliable current reasoning boolean from these sources.

sources.title: Models.dev Nova Lite record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead inspected and its AWS links followed; not used as independent primary verification.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. All authors were affiliated with Amazon at publication. Table 1, PDF page 6, lists Nova Lite with Params NP and 300k context; NP is not expanded in the inspected text, so this is recorded literally as a nonnumeric entry. There is no separate active-parameter column. The table supplies no newly disclosed nominal size.

sources.title: PHLoRA: data-free Post-hoc Low-Rank Adapter extraction from full-rank checkpoint
sources.publisher: Amazon AGI authors / NeurIPS 2025 Efficient Reasoning Workshop
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. Evaluates Nova Micro, Lite and Pro full-rank fine-tuning and adapter extraction. Appendix B names Lite/Pro attention and MLP target modules; ranks 32/64/512 describe adapters, not model parameter counts. Neither total nor active Lite count is reported. Adapter pruning in these experiments does not establish a pruned production Lite architecture.

sources.title: Fine-tune Nova 1.0 - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. Run configuration maps amazon.nova-lite-v1:0:300k to base path nova-lite/prod. Full-rank and LoRA recipes disclose training hyperparameters and instance counts, but no nominal size or active count and no different named size-disclosed base from which Lite could inherit a count.

sources.title: Continued pre-training (CPT) on Nova 2.0 on SageMaker HyperPod
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. Explicitly describes Nova Lite 2.0 as a larger model than Nova Lite 1.0 and names base path nova-lite-2/prod. No numeric size is provided. This structural size distinction defeats transferring any Nova 2 Lite size to the original Lite merely from the shared tier name.

sources.title: Amazon Nova (formerly Olympus)
sources.evidence: Secondary lead inspected October 27 solely to check provenance of the approximately 20B Lite claim surfaced by search. The page explicitly labels its parameter figures estimates based on benchmark scores; it is not a developer disclosure or a named-base lineage specification. Not accepted as a catalog count.

name.note: Official model name; Amazon branding is already represented by the developer field.

developer.note: Developed by Amazon; technical report credits Amazon Artificial General Intelligence.

family.note: Normalized family key for Amazon Nova. Lite is the model tier; baseline nova-lite splits the documented Nova family.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public general availability announcement is December 3. Current Bedrock card lists December 5 without explaining the difference; do not replace the contemporaneous public release with that later listing date.

open_weights.note: AWS explicitly calls the family including Lite proprietary; current training documentation also says Nova weights remain proprietary. SageMaker broad table placement under Open-Weight Models is inconsistent, and is not evidence of a downloadable weight release.

license.note: Exact Nova Lite listing names AWS Service Terms. This is proprietary service usage licensing, not an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review reopened the original evidence and searched AWS/Amazon Science for nominal size and newer comparison tables. MASSIVE-Agents Table 1 records Lite Params as NP; the Nova 2 tables and PHLoRA study disclose no numeric size. Current recipes name nova-lite/prod without a sized parent; Premier/Pro distillation is not an equal-size lineage. AWS explicitly says Nova 2 Lite is larger than Nova 1 Lite, so no same-name size transfer is supported. The surfaced ~20B claim is an explicitly benchmark-derived secondary estimate. No supported nominal total was found; null is not due to requiring a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Checked active parameters independently. The later MASSIVE-Agents table has no active-parameter column, Nova 2 comparison tables report capabilities, and PHLoRA reports adapter ranks and evaluation scores rather than activated parameters. No first-party nominal active-per-token count was found in original reports or current customization documentation. Dense/MoE topology is still unestablished; neither adapter module names nor an unknown total supplies an active count.

architecture.note: Transformer is explicit. Dense versus mixture-of-experts topology and detailed configuration remain undisclosed; this value makes no sparsity claim.

context_window.note: 300K tokens in the exact v1 Lite column, confirmed by the migration comparison.

modalities.note: Text/image/video are native listed inputs; PDF is supported as document input through Converse. Text is the output modality; no audio input is asserted from the shared schema.

reasoning.note: Meaning is dedicated extended thinking, not general problem-solving capability. Exact Nova 1 Lite migration table says No, but the current v1 request schema explicitly documents reasoningConfig for Lite. Clear the baseline false pending resolution of this first-party contradiction.

tool_call.note: Exact Bedrock model card supports client-side tool calling; original report evaluates Lite function calling. Nova 2 built-in tools are a separate capability.

description.value: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
description.note: Summary of documented inputs, output, context and tool calling without speed or price claims.

patch.description: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
patch.notes: Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; later Amazon comparison tables provide no numeric size. Transformer architecture is confirmed; dense versus MoE topology is unknown. Public GA was December 3, 2024, despite the current Bedrock card listing December 5. Dedicated reasoning remains unresolved: the AWS migration table says Nova 1 Lite has no extended thinking, while the v1 API schema documents reasoningConfig for Lite. AWS classifies Nova as proprietary; the audit records inconsistent SageMaker table grouping.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after reopening original reports, the Premier addendum, Nova 2 comparisons and current AWS cards, then checking MASSIVE-Agents, PHLoRA and customization documentation. No nominal disclosure or sized base lineage was found; MASSIVE-Agents uses NP, Nova 2 Lite is explicitly larger, and the ~20B secondary claim is a benchmark estimate. Preserved all other audited fields: December 3 public launch, proprietary licensing, Transformer architecture, 300K multimodal/PDF input and tool calling; existing reasoning-source conflict remains unresolved.
